parsed_payload.verified_states: Before the error, the student correctly has A+B+C=180°, all angles acute; X lies on the angle bisector so ∠XBC=B/2; and O is the circumcenter so ∠BOC=2A=2n. The cyclicity conclusion ∠BOC=∠BXC is valid here because O and X both lie inside the acute triangle, hence on the same side of BC.
parsed_payload.error_reason: The student incorrectly sets ∠XCB=90°. X lying on the altitude from C means CX is perpendicular to AB, not to CB.
parsed_payload.new_direction: Use CX⊥AB to derive ∠XCB=90°−B, then compute ∠BXC=90°+B/2 and equate it with ∠BOC=2n.
parsed_payload.reasoning: Let A=n, B=B, C=C. Since X is on the angle bisector, ∠XBC=B/2. Since CX is the altitude to AB, CX⊥AB, so the angle between CX and CB is 90°−B; hence ∠XCB=90°−B. Therefore ∠BXC=180°−B/2−(90°−B)=90°+B/2. Because O and X are inside the acute triangle, they are on the same side of BC, so cyclicity of B,O,X,C gives ∠BOC=∠BXC. Also ∠BOC=2A=2n. Thus 2n=90°+B/2, so B=4n−180°. Then C=180°−n−B=360°−5n. Acuteness requires B<90° and C<90°, giving 4n−180<90 ⇒ n<67.5 and 360−5n<90 ⇒ n>54. Therefore the largest possible integer n is 67.
